button.label: New block
button.screentip: Insert a code block
button.supertip: Adds an empty dark code block at the default size, ready to type into.

button.label: Code block
button.screentip: Insert a listing
button.supertip: An ordinary code block: syntax colours, no prompts.

button.label: Transcript
button.screentip: Insert a session at an interpreter
button.supertip: A block that is a transcript from the start. Type the session into it and press Stylize: every line gets the prompt, once. After that a newly typed line stays bare until you press Prompt, and Output takes a prompt off.

button.label: Stylize
button.screentip: Stylize the selected block
button.supertip: Re-colors the selected code block from scratch. Safe to press as often as you like.

button.label: Strip
button.screentip: Return the block to plain text
button.supertip: Removes the colours, emphasis, numbers and guides. The block stays, and Stylize brings it all back.

button.label: Copy code
button.screentip: Copy the block's code to the clipboard
button.supertip: Copies the text, not the shape, so pasting into an editor gives you the source.

checkBox.label: Indent guides
checkBox.screentip: Show or hide the indent guides
checkBox.supertip: The vertical lines marking each level of nesting. Off by default.

checkBox.label: Line numbers
checkBox.supertip: Numbers live in their own shape, so the code text stays pure source.

editBox.label: First line
editBox.screentip: The number the first line gets
editBox.supertip: For code split across several slides: set the second slide's block to start at 24 and its numbers carry on from the first. Stored per block. Setting it turns the line numbers on, since a start number with no numbers showing does nothing.

comboBox.label: Size
comboBox.supertip: Pick a rung or type any size. Refused if the block would stop fitting the slide.

button.label: Larger
button.screentip: Step up the size ladder
button.supertip: Stops growing where the code would stop fitting the slide.

button.label: Smaller
button.screentip: Step down the size ladder

button.label: Fit
button.screentip: Pick the largest size that fits
button.supertip: Warns instead of shrinking silently when the code will not read from the back of the room.

button.label: Emphasize
button.screentip: Emphasize the selected lines
button.supertip: Select text inside the block and press this to band those lines. With the block itself selected rather than text, it clears the emphasis. The choice is stored on the block, so duplicating the slide and moving the emphasis down a line is two clicks.

button.label: Arrow
button.screentip: Point at a line from the left margin
button.supertip: Puts a block arrow beside one line and leaves the code at full contrast, which is what you want when the whole snippet has to stay readable. Uses the line the cursor is on, or - with the block itself selected - the emphasised line. Press it again on the same line to take it away, or with the block selected and nothing emphasised to clear them all.

checkBox.label: Transcript
checkBox.screentip: This block is a session at an interpreter
checkBox.supertip: Puts the language's prompt in front of every line you typed - >>> for Python, and ... on the body of a statement. Blank lines and lines marked as Output get none. The prompt goes into the text, so nothing can drift out of alignment with it, and Copy code strips it back off.

button.label: Prompt
button.screentip: These lines were typed at the interpreter
button.supertip: Puts the prompt back on the lines you select. A line you have just typed starts without one, which is to say it counts as output, so this is how you promote it. A bare cursor is enough for one line.

button.label: Output
button.screentip: These lines were printed by the interpreter
button.supertip: Takes the prompt off the lines you select, which is what makes them output: they lose their syntax color and their line number, because a printed value is not code. Pressing it on a block that is not yet a transcript makes it one first, so marking your first output line is a single press. Use Prompt to put a line back. A bare cursor is enough for one line.

button.label: Note
button.screentip: Attach a note to a line of code
button.supertip: Puts a note beside the block with a line pointing at the code, so you can say what a line does without cramming it into a comment. Uses the line the cursor is on, or - with the block itself selected - the emphasised line, which makes annotating a walkthrough one click per slide. It stays anchored: change the size or edit the code above it and Stylize keeps it level with its line.

button.label: Output
button.screentip: Attach what the code printed to a line
button.supertip: A note dressed as a terminal - the code font, a darker panel and a green arrow - so it reads as output rather than as an aside. Uses the line the cursor is on, or the emphasised line with the block itself selected. Long output wraps flush with the first character after the arrow, not under it.

button.label: Delete note
button.screentip: Delete the note you have singled out
button.supertip: Removes the note on the line your cursor is on, or the note you have clicked into, along with its connector. Same rule as the color and size controls, so there is one answer to which note is meant. To remove every note on a block at once, press Note with the block itself selected - that one asks first.

button.label: Step through
button.screentip: One slide per line, each emphasising the next
button.supertip: Duplicates this slide once per line of code, emphasising a different line each time. This slide keeps nothing emphasised, so it still shows the code whole. Select text first to walk only those lines.

button.label: Build up
button.screentip: One slide per line, emphasis growing downward
button.supertip: The same, except each slide emphasises everything up to the current line rather than just that line. For building code up rather than tracing it.

button.label: Point at
button.screentip: One slide per line, an arrow moving down the margin
button.supertip: Like Step through, but it points at each line from the left margin instead of fading the rest - so the code stays whole and readable throughout. For tracing execution on a snippet short enough that every line should stay legible.

checkBox.label: Note per step
checkBox.screentip: Give every generated slide a note
checkBox.supertip: Each slide the walkthrough builds arrives with a note already attached to the line it emphasises, so you fill them in rather than clicking to create them. Build up attaches it to the newest line.

button.label: Hide lines
button.screentip: Hide the selected lines behind a question mark
button.supertip: Select lines inside the block and press this to cover them, keeping their space. Ask the class what belongs there. With the block itself selected rather than text, it reveals them again.

button.label: Reveal next
button.screentip: Add the answer on the next slide
button.supertip: Duplicates this slide with nothing hidden, so the reveal follows the question.

comboBox.label: Note size
comboBox.supertip: Auto sizes each note from the block it belongs to. Pick a rung or type any size to pin it instead. Applies to the note on the line your cursor is on, or the note you have clicked into. With nothing singled out it only records the choice for the next note, so opening this list can never repaint a note you were not pointing at. Each of the three note controls changes only what it is named after, so notes on one slide can differ. The choice is also remembered for notes made afterwards.

dropDown.label: Note color
dropDown.supertip: The first six are quiet, for a note that is an aside about the code; the rest are saturated, for one that should be the loudest thing on the slide. Applies to the note on the line your cursor is on, or the note you have clicked into. With nothing singled out it only records the choice for the next note, so opening this list can never repaint a note you were not pointing at. Each of the three note controls changes only what it is named after, so notes on one slide can differ. The text color follows the fill, so a light preset gets dark words.

button.screentip: The color notes are set to
button.supertip: Shows the color currently chosen, and applies it to the note you have singled out - by putting the cursor on its line, or by clicking into it. Press it to give a second note the same color as the first without going back through the list.

dropDown.label: Note font
dropDown.supertip: Deck default inherits your presentation's own body font, so a note looks like the rest of the deck rather than like code. It cannot be applied back to a note that already has a named font, so it only affects notes made afterwards. The others ship with Windows or Office, and apply to the note on the line your cursor is on, or the note you have clicked into, and otherwise only to notes made afterwards.

dropDown.label: Arrow color
dropDown.supertip: The syntax colors, darkened until they read on a white slide - the palette itself is chosen against the block background and looks faded on one. Arrows are uniform by design, so this repaints every arrow in the presentation, not only the ones in front of you.

button.screentip: The color arrows are set to
button.supertip: Shows the color in use. Press it to repaint every arrow in the presentation with it, which is worth doing after recoloring one by hand.

dropDown.label: Language
dropDown.supertip: Sets which lexer the Stylize button uses. Stored on the shape, so each block remembers its own language.
